Author: Casey Zaitz, Lead of PMaaS & Organizational Transformation at M&S Consulting

You know a system is bad when engineers and scientists—people who solve complex problems for a living—would rather deal with paperwork than use the existing software. That was the case for an internal SharePoint site used to manage a research and development safety review process. The SharePoint site, which housed hundreds of documents for over 100 active projects, pushed the limits of SharePoint and its users, becoming cumbersome for both researchers and managers. Even with a special reporting feature built to track extensive matrixed training requirements, using the site actively made life more complicated for the research teams. And if you’ve ever met a scientist or engineer, you know they don’t have time for inefficient administrative tasks.
So, when the request came to “fix this,” our answer was a resounding yes—but also, yikes. Because let me tell you, this wasn’t just a minor facelift. This was a full-scale rescue mission.
The Problem: A Tangle of Red Tape and Spreadsheets
Imagine this: You’re a scientist trying to push the boundaries of research. You need to conduct an updated safety review and obtain a new operations permit every time you make a change to your experiment design. It’s 2023, and the existing system for obtaining a permit for safe operations in an R&D environment is still running on SharePoint 2013 (yes, really), utilizing InfoPath forms (RIP).
“Running” is a misnomer: it was slow, it was rigid, and it required multiple tracking spreadsheets, manual approvals via email across different departments, and reporting based on data calls to dozens of project leads. Every time something changed—like a new chemical being introduced to a project—scientists had to go back through the entire process, again and again. Multiply that by 100+ projects happening at once, and you get a recipe for frustration, inefficiency, and a lot of people quietly screaming into their lab coats.
The Solution: Fix It, But Make It Fast
Now, you’d think an overhaul of this scale would take years. The problem was, the essential SharePoint site was already on life support. There weren’t years to spare. Something was needed now.
That’s where we came in. My role? Map out every single step of this process, identify gaps and bottlenecks, and recommend improvements. And when I say “map,” I mean a literal 17-foot scroll of plotter paper covered in process diagrams. (If you ever need to get a bunch of people to agree on something, I highly recommend a massive, intimidating process map.)
I spent eight months interviewing scientists, administrators, safety officers, managers, and support contractors—anyone who had a role in the process—to determine exactly where things were breaking down. And let me tell you, the pain points were everywhere.
But the key to this project’s success? The business owner was all in. She didn’t just want a new app; she wanted a real solution. She made tough calls, streamlined decision-making, and was willing to prioritize what was necessary for launch versus what could be phased in later. Despite a hectic schedule, she made time to attend daily scrum meetings and provide feedback and answers to questions.
The Build: Small Team, Big Impact
Once the process mapping was digested, I created a blueprint of wireframes for screens, including landing pages, digitized forms, a searchable document management page, and database interface pages. We incorporated feedback and gained client approval on several of those pages, and it was time to build. Enter Nick and Josh, our development power duo—one tackling backend, the other frontend. And let’s not forget our IT project manager, who kept this project moving without bringing 20 people to every meeting—a miracle in itself.
Together, this small but mighty team:
✅ Consolidated multiple systems into one streamlined application✅ Digitized critical forms and processes✅ Built a database that could actually generate useful reports (instead of requiring hours of manual data hunting)✅ Integrated work orders directly into the system, eliminating unnecessary back-and-forth between teams✅ Simplified training tracking, ensuring researchers had the proper certifications before working on projects✅ Migrated data and documents from the old system to the new, ensuring researchers did not need to re-create all their permitted project records
And the best part? We achieved this at a fraction of the cost of comparable projects elsewhere.
The Result: A System That Works—Finally
So, where are we now?
The application is up and running. The process is smoother, approvals are faster, and the system doesn’t actively make people’s jobs harder. Researchers are actually using it—and that’s the real test of success.
Even better? The new system is designed for scalability. Similar organizations can now obtain the solution and adapt it to their specific needs without the massive price tag. We’re continuing to develop additional modules and are excited to help adjust this operations application more broadly across the public sector.
What’s Next?
The work isn’t done yet. Now that people have seen what’s possible, they want in. We’re already expanding the app to handle additional permitting processes for facility use, as well as additional document management requirements and construction safety approvals.
We fixed a broken system. And we did it efficiently and at a cost that makes sense. And if you ask me? That’s the kind of work that makes all those months of process mapping, interviews, and wireframing 100% worth it.
If you’ve got a system that’s making people miserable, let’s talk. We might just be able to help you empower your operations.
 
 Contact M&S Consulting:

item.title: What Powers Digital Transformation Success in Law Firms
item.dc:creator: LeoTome
item.content:encoded:
When I talk to law firm leaders about digital transformation, one of the first things I emphasize is this: technology alone isn't enough. To drive real, lasting change, firms need a clear strategy grounded in strong pillars—pillars that align technology, people, and business goals into a single, unstoppable force.Without these pillars, digital transformation efforts often crumble under their own weight.

Let’s dive into what makes a law firm’s transformation strategy truly successful.

1. Defining Clear Objectives

You can't hit a target you can't see.

Before a single new tool is implemented, firms must define what they’re trying to achieve. Are you aiming to:

  • Deliver a more seamless and responsive client experience?
  • Streamline internal operations to cut costs and boost productivity?
  • Open new revenue streams through innovative services?

In my experience, successful transformations are laser-focused on two or three primary goals—not a laundry list of "nice to haves."

Clear objectives allow you to prioritize investments, measure success, and keep everyone aligned when the inevitable bumps in the road appear.

2. Leadership and Culture: The Real Drivers of Change

I can't overstate how important leadership buy-in is.

If the managing partners or executive committee aren't truly committed—beyond a one-time announcement—transformation will sputter. Leaders must be visible champions of change, modeling the behaviors and mindsets they want the rest of the firm to adopt.

Just as crucial: cultivating a culture that embraces innovation, experimentation, and continuous improvement.

Firms that treat transformation as "someone else's project" —often the IT department's responsibility—will fail. The most successful firms make transformation part of everyone's job.

3. Aligning Technology with Business Goals

It's easy to get dazzled by tech trends. I see firms all the time buying expensive AI tools, blockchain systems, or fancy CRM platforms without a real plan for how those tools drive business value.

The technology should be the servant of the firm's strategic objectives, not the master.

For example, if your objective is to improve client response time, maybe the best investment isn't a massive AI initiative—maybe it's a simple workflow automation tool that speeds up intake and conflict checks.

Technology decisions must always tie back to the core business case.

4. Data-Driven Decision Making

In the past, law firms often relied on gut feel and experience to guide strategy.

Today, the best firms pair that experience with hard data. They use client feedback, operational metrics, financial dashboards, and predictive analytics to make smarter, faster decisions.

The lesson I've learned again and again: You can't manage what you can't measure.

5. Managing Change Proactively

Resistance to change is human nature. In law firms, it’s practically an art form.

That’s why change management needs to be baked into your strategy from day one—not bolted on after the fact.

I’ve found that the firms who succeed are the ones who:

  • Involve stakeholders early and often
  • Communicate transparently and frequently
  • Offer plenty of training and support
  • Celebrate small wins along the way

When people feel informed, involved, and supported, they’re much more likely to become allies rather than obstacles.

Final Thoughts

Building a successful digital transformation strategy isn’t about chasing technology for its own sake. It's about:

  • Getting crystal clear on your goals.
  • Making transformation a leadership and cultural priority.
  • Choosing technologies that align with real business needs.
  • Embracing data-driven decision making.
  • Managing the human side of change with care and purpose.

Law firms that build on these pillars aren't just adopting new tools—they're building a better future.

And the firms that start now? They'll be the ones setting the pace for the next decade of legal innovation.

In the next post, we'll dig deeper into what it really means to become a data-driven law firm—and why that's such a game-changer.

item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Why Microsoft Still Leads in the Enterprise

Microsoft isn’t just a familiar name in the business world. For many organizations, it’s the backbone of daily operations, strategic planning, and innovation. In this episode of Human-Coded, M&S Consulting leaders Cody Childers and Ashok Aggarwal break down why Microsoft continues to be a compelling choice for enterprise technology needs.

What makes Microsoft stand out? It's a mix of ubiquity, integration, innovation, and user empowerment:

  • Widespread adoption: Microsoft tools are already used across most organizations—from Windows operating systems to Excel, Teams, SharePoint, and Azure.
  • Integrated ecosystem: Tools like Power BI, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform are built to work seamlessly with one another, cutting down on complexity and reducing the need for third-party plugins.
  • Reliable innovation: Microsoft is known for introducing future-ready features without compromising on stability, making it a dependable choice for large-scale organizations.
  • User-first tools: From advanced dev platforms like VS Code and .NET to the ever-reliable Excel, Microsoft supports both technical and non-technical users with tools that are powerful and intuitive.

Innovation Without the Risk

Microsoft strikes a unique balance between innovation and operational reliability. It’s not just about being first to market—it's about delivering updates that make life easier for enterprises. Key examples include:

  • Azure’s rapid growth, rivaling AWS
  • The resurgence of Microsoft 365 and Teams
  • Continuous improvement in security and identity tools through Entra and Azure AD
  • Integration with OpenAI, enabling enterprise-ready AI experiences

This thoughtful, steady approach to change allows organizations to modernize at their own pace without jeopardizing security or productivity.

The Power of Hidden Value

While Microsoft’s flagship products are widely recognized, many other offerings are underutilized or underappreciated:

  • SQL Server and .NET continue to provide high-performance and scalable platforms for enterprise application development
  • TypeScript, a Microsoft creation, has become a staple of modern web development
  • VS Code has grown into one of the most beloved development environments globally
  • Excel, with its decades of enhancements, remains foundational to enterprise decision-making

These tools are not just powerful individually—they’re even more impactful when used together.

Looking Ahead

Microsoft’s continued relevance in a rapidly changing tech landscape is not accidental. It’s the result of intentional product development, ecosystem cohesion, and an understanding of enterprise needs. For organizations aiming to stay agile without sacrificing stability, Microsoft remains a smart, future-ready foundation.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
As businesses navigate the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), it becomes increasingly crucial to assess how AI can be effectively integrated into their strategies. AI is not a one-size-fits-all solution; rather, it should be seen as an extension of a company’s existing technological framework, enhancing current capabilities and adding value to strategic objectives.

Aligning AI with Business Strategy

To integrate AI effectively, businesses should start by ensuring that their existing technology plans and infrastructure are robust. AI is not a standalone tool; it must build on a foundation of reliable data and secure networks. Companies should first evaluate their current systems to ensure that they are capable of supporting AI. This includes having standardized data and effective reporting mechanisms in place. If a company struggles to provide accurate data to its management team, AI won’t be the solution to these underlying issues.

The next step is to identify specific objectives that AI can help achieve. These goals should be rooted in the company’s overall business strategy. Whether it’s enhancing customer experience, streamlining operations, or driving data-driven decisions, clear objectives are essential. AI is most effective when it complements existing strategies, acting as a catalyst rather than a replacement.

Navigating the Regulatory Environment

The regulatory landscape for AI is complex and varies by industry and region. However, businesses must take a proactive approach to understanding and complying with these regulations. The European AI Act, for example, places significant responsibility on organizations to ensure their AI systems meet ethical and privacy standards. This responsibility cannot be shifted onto vendors; businesses must rigorously test and validate their AI solutions before deployment.

Understanding the level of risk associated with AI systems is also critical. High-risk AI systems, particularly those used in healthcare, education, or law enforcement, require stringent oversight and governance. Compliance should not be viewed as a mere tick-box exercise; instead, it’s an opportunity to build trust and establish a reputation for ethical AI practices. This involves not only meeting regulatory requirements but also fostering a culture of transparency and inclusivity in AI development.

Implementing AI with Ethical Considerations

Successful AI integration requires a multi-faceted approach that includes design, testing, and continuous monitoring. During the design phase, it’s essential to involve a diverse group of stakeholders who represent the various groups impacted by the AI system. This ensures that the system is designed with a broad perspective, addressing potential biases and ethical concerns from the outset.

Rigorous testing is crucial to identify and mitigate any issues before deployment. Unlike traditional systems, AI requires a more nuanced approach to testing, as it must account for the different ways users may interact with the system. Continuous monitoring post-deployment is equally important. AI systems must adapt to changing environments and usage patterns, ensuring they remain effective and reliable over time.

Building a Trustworthy AI Framework

AI implementation is similar to information security in many ways. Both require a risk-based approach, early involvement of key stakeholders, and a commitment to ongoing governance and monitoring. For AI, this means developing clear policies and guidelines around its use, ensuring ethical considerations are embedded in the process, and maintaining oversight to prevent issues as the business environment evolves.

Integrating AI into your business strategy isn’t just about adopting the latest technology—it's about setting the stage for a transformative journey. As you navigate this dynamic landscape, remember that AI is a powerful ally that can elevate your capabilities and drive meaningful progress. It’s not about replacing what works; it’s about enhancing and expanding what’s possible.

By aligning AI with your strategic goals, staying ahead of regulatory requirements, and embedding ethical considerations into every phase, you’re not just adopting a tool—you’re championing a future where technology and humanity thrive together. Embrace this opportunity to redefine your approach, drive innovation, and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

Let’s transform the future together. Reach out to us to explore how AI can align with your unique vision and propel your business towards unprecedented success. Our team is here to guide you through every step, ensuring that your AI journey is as impactful and rewarding as it can be. 

Ready to make AI a game-changer for your business? Contact us today to start a conversation about how we can help you integrate AI in a way that’s strategic, ethical, and uniquely tailored to your needs.

item.title: Human Coded 013: AI & the Microsoft Ecosystem: A Business Leader’s Guide
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Why Microsoft’s Approach to AI Stands Out

AI isn’t new to Microsoft. Long before the hype around ChatGPT, Microsoft was integrating machine learning and analytics capabilities into Azure. What makes today’s AI strategy so powerful is Microsoft’s full-stack approach:

  • Deep integration of AI into Office 365, Windows, and enterprise tools
  • Exclusive cloud provider relationship with OpenAI
  • Support for AI hardware with built-in Neural Processing Units (NPUs)
  • Secure access to enterprise data through tools like SharePoint, Cosmos DB, and Entra ID

This means Microsoft isn’t just layering AI on top of its existing products. It’s embedding intelligence at the core of everyday workflows.

Meeting People Where They Work

Rather than requiring new tools or steep learning curves, Microsoft is putting AI directly into the tools employees already use. This includes:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot for productivity apps like Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • GitHub Copilot for code generation and review
  • Windows OS enhancements with built-in AI assistants

For most users, these embedded tools will account for nearly all their AI usage, without needing to master prompt engineering or custom integrations.

GitHub Copilot: AI for Developers

GitHub is one of the most popular code-hosting platforms in the world, and now it's home to some of the most promising developments in AI-assisted software development. GitHub Copilot helps:

  • Generate multi-language code snippets
  • Identify bugs and logic flaws
  • Accelerate development cycles by providing useful starting points

This changes the role of the developer from writing every line of code to designing smarter, faster workflows.

Azure OpenAI Service: Secure, Scalable AI Infrastructure

Azure gives businesses private, secure access to OpenAI’s models, without sending proprietary data to public systems. Key benefits include:

  • Dedicated tenant environments to isolate data
  • Enterprise-grade privacy and compliance
  • Flexible usage: spin up environments for a project, extract value, and shut them down

Azure empowers organizations to build intelligent tools with their own domain-specific content, internal documents, and customer data.

The Road to Agentic AI

While fully autonomous AI agents are still emerging, Microsoft’s tools are already laying the groundwork. Through Power Automate, Power Apps, and logic-driven workflows, companies can begin automating repeatable processes today.

Agentic AI will mature, but for now, businesses should:

  • Start with automation of known workflows
  • Invest in better data hygiene and structure
  • Build foundational understanding across teams

How to Get Started

For leaders ready to explore AI within Microsoft’s ecosystem, the first step is creating shared understanding. AI means different things to different people, and Microsoft’s naming conventions (e.g., “Copilot”) can vary widely across services.

Jay Mason recommends starting with:

  • Teamwide AI education to establish a shared vocabulary
  • Small, targeted use cases like document classification or data extraction
  • Evaluation of internal readiness for automation and AI-driven decisions

Once those foundations are laid, the leap to agentic AI or custom models becomes more practical.

The Future of Enterprise AI with Microsoft

Over the next few years, expect Microsoft’s AI capabilities to:

  • Become more intuitive and less reliant on structured prompts
  • Expand multimodal features, combining text, visuals, audio, and more
  • Deepen identity-based access control for personalized AI agents
  • Require stronger monitoring and oversight to track model performance

AI isn’t a silver bullet, but when combined with Microsoft’s mature stack and enterprise-grade infrastructure, it becomes a meaningful tool for transformation.

item.title: Human Coded 014: The Change Equation - People, Process, and Technology
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Why Change Management Matters More Than Ever

Technology may be the catalyst for transformation, but it’s not the reason projects succeed-or fail. In this episode of Human-Coded, Casey Zaitz, Director of Agile Project Management and Organizational Transformation at M&S Consulting, breaks down what makes change stick in modern organizations.

The Three Pillars of Effective Change

Successful transformation happens when organizations balance three distinct but interdependent types of change:

  • Technology Change Management: Focused on the platforms, systems, and tools being implemented. It’s the most straightforward but only works when paired with the other two.
  • Process Change Management: Looks at how work gets done, identifying inefficiencies, redefining workflows, and building alignment across teams.
  • People Change Management: The most overlooked yet most critical. It ensures employees are supported, involved, and prepared for the shift-not just told what’s changing.

Without people-centered strategies, even the most sophisticated tools will fail to deliver value.

Why Change Initiatives Fail

Many organizations struggle with change because key decisions are made in silos. Teams operate with different assumptions, communication is limited, and critical stakeholders-especially upstream and downstream teams-aren’t included in the planning. This leads to misalignment, resistance, and missed opportunities for impact.

Casey highlights that bringing the right voices into the room early can transform resistance into advocacy. Inclusion builds ownership, which in turn drives adoption.

Blueprinting for Better Outcomes

To solve these pain points, M&S Consulting developed the Process Impact Blueprinting Workshop, a two-and-a-half-day collaborative session designed to:

  • Unite stakeholders across departments
  • Identify points of friction and opportunity
  • Map out current vs. future state workflows
  • Establish shared goals and language around change

These workshops give teams a tangible, strategic foundation to guide the tactical work ahead. They also create space to address skepticism, invite feedback, and build consensus.

Advice for Leaders Getting Started

If you’re a leader preparing for a transformation, here are some practical first steps:

  • Establish urgency: Communicate why the change matters now.
  • Build a coalition: Secure buy-in across executive and operational leadership.
  • Define short-term wins: Identify early outcomes that build momentum and morale.
  • Anchor change in culture: Embed adaptability into how the organization operates-not just what it delivers.

Avoid change fatigue by sequencing efforts realistically. Trying to do everything at once often results in burnout and lower adoption.

Common Misconceptions

The biggest misconception? That technology alone is enough. As Casey puts it, technology is the enabler-but people are the difference-maker. Focusing solely on systems while overlooking the human side of change is a costly mistake. Change is inevitable, but successful change is intentional.

item.title: Human Coded 015: Turning Resistance into Buy-In - The Art of People Change Management
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Understanding Resistance as a Resource

Resistance to change is often seen as a barrier, but it’s also a signal. As Casey Zaitz and Alexander Wenzel explain, resistance can reveal overlooked risks, broken processes, and communication gaps that would otherwise remain hidden. Rather than suppressing skepticism, organizations can embrace it as a path to alignment.

Team members who voice concerns are often deeply invested in their work. They know where the breakdowns happen and where the stakes are highest. Listening to them builds trust and surfaces insights that can strengthen the initiative.

Turning Skeptics into Advocates

M&S Consulting’s Process Impact Blueprinting Workshop is designed to do just that—bring the right people into the room from the beginning. By including not just the core team but also upstream and downstream stakeholders, the process builds shared ownership and surfaces interdependencies.

Leaders shouldn’t shy away from involving skeptics. In fact, those with the most hesitation often become the strongest champions—once their input is heard and their expertise is validated. One client, initially reluctant and vocal about past failed initiatives, became a key voice in driving change forward after realizing the broader impact of their team’s work.

Why People Must Come First

Projects don’t fail because the tech doesn’t work. They fail because people don’t adopt it. That’s why people change management isn’t just one of three pillars—it’s the foundation. Key success factors include:

  • Early involvement: Bring in voices from every affected department
  • Active listening: Validate concerns, even when they can’t be acted on immediately
  • Transparent communication: Explain the why behind the what
  • Empowerment through ownership: Let users help shape the future state

When people are included in the design process, they’re far more likely to support implementation.

The Role of the Project Manager

Project managers are uniquely positioned to bridge communication gaps. They’re often the only team members who speak with stakeholders at every level—from frontline users to the C-suite. A good project manager can spot misalignment early, elevate overlooked voices, and keep teams moving forward with empathy and clarity.

This role becomes especially important when leadership unintentionally sidelines critical team members or when contributors feel their concerns are ignored. A project manager’s ability to notice and address that dynamic can make the difference between adoption and disengagement.

Building Trust Through Culture

Trust is the currency of change. Leaders can build or rebuild it by:

  • Maintaining transparency, even when the news is difficult
  • Demonstrating empathy for the daily realities of employees
  • Involving people meaningfully—not just notifying them after decisions are made
  • Clarifying that change is a shared journey, not a top-down decree

The Human Operating System

Casey introduces the idea of a “human operating system”—a metaphor for how people process change much like a complex software environment. Just like a codebase, it needs:

  • Clear architecture (communication structure)
  • Continuous feedback (listening and adaptation)
  • Debugging (identifying and resolving misalignment)
  • Regular updates (ongoing support and training)

Neglecting this system leads to friction, burnout, and hidden resistance. But when it’s nurtured, it becomes a powerful engine for transformation.

As businesses navigate the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), it becomes increasingly crucial to assess how AI can be effectively integrated into their strategies. AI is not a one-size-fits-all solution; rather, it should be seen as an extension of a company’s existing technological framework, enhancing current capabilities and adding value to strategic objectives.

Aligning AI with Business Strategy

To integrate AI effectively, businesses should start by ensuring that their existing technology plans and infrastructure are robust. AI is not a standalone tool; it must build on a foundation of reliable data and secure networks. Companies should first evaluate their current systems to ensure that they are capable of supporting AI. This includes having standardized data and effective reporting mechanisms in place. If a company struggles to provide accurate data to its management team, AI won’t be the solution to these underlying issues.

The next step is to identify specific objectives that AI can help achieve. These goals should be rooted in the company’s overall business strategy. Whether it’s enhancing customer experience, streamlining operations, or driving data-driven decisions, clear objectives are essential. AI is most effective when it complements existing strategies, acting as a catalyst rather than a replacement.

Navigating the Regulatory Environment

The regulatory landscape for AI is complex and varies by industry and region. However, businesses must take a proactive approach to understanding and complying with these regulations. The European AI Act, for example, places significant responsibility on organizations to ensure their AI systems meet ethical and privacy standards. This responsibility cannot be shifted onto vendors; businesses must rigorously test and validate their AI solutions before deployment.

Understanding the level of risk associated with AI systems is also critical. High-risk AI systems, particularly those used in healthcare, education, or law enforcement, require stringent oversight and governance. Compliance should not be viewed as a mere tick-box exercise; instead, it’s an opportunity to build trust and establish a reputation for ethical AI practices. This involves not only meeting regulatory requirements but also fostering a culture of transparency and inclusivity in AI development.

Implementing AI with Ethical Considerations

Successful AI integration requires a multi-faceted approach that includes design, testing, and continuous monitoring. During the design phase, it’s essential to involve a diverse group of stakeholders who represent the various groups impacted by the AI system. This ensures that the system is designed with a broad perspective, addressing potential biases and ethical concerns from the outset.

Rigorous testing is crucial to identify and mitigate any issues before deployment. Unlike traditional systems, AI requires a more nuanced approach to testing, as it must account for the different ways users may interact with the system. Continuous monitoring post-deployment is equally important. AI systems must adapt to changing environments and usage patterns, ensuring they remain effective and reliable over time.

Building a Trustworthy AI Framework

AI implementation is similar to information security in many ways. Both require a risk-based approach, early involvement of key stakeholders, and a commitment to ongoing governance and monitoring. For AI, this means developing clear policies and guidelines around its use, ensuring ethical considerations are embedded in the process, and maintaining oversight to prevent issues as the business environment evolves.

Integrating AI into your business strategy isn’t just about adopting the latest technology—it's about setting the stage for a transformative journey. As you navigate this dynamic landscape, remember that AI is a powerful ally that can elevate your capabilities and drive meaningful progress. It’s not about replacing what works; it’s about enhancing and expanding what’s possible.

By aligning AI with your strategic goals, staying ahead of regulatory requirements, and embedding ethical considerations into every phase, you’re not just adopting a tool—you’re championing a future where technology and humanity thrive together. Embrace this opportunity to redefine your approach, drive innovation, and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

Let’s transform the future together. Reach out to us to explore how AI can align with your unique vision and propel your business towards unprecedented success. Our team is here to guide you through every step, ensuring that your AI journey is as impactful and rewarding as it can be. 

Ready to make AI a game-changer for your business? Contact us today to start a conversation about how we can help you integrate AI in a way that’s strategic, ethical, and uniquely tailored to your needs.

item.title: Human Coded 016: Blueprinting Organizational Change Management for Real Results
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Moving from Vision to Execution

Organizational change isn’t just about launching new technology or reworking a process. It’s about aligning vision, securing buy-in, and empowering every level of the company to move in the same direction. In this episode of Human-Coded, Casey Zaitz walks through the structure and strategy behind organizational change management—especially how M&S Consulting uses process blueprinting to turn ideas into action.

Urgency Without Burnout

Creating urgency is key to momentum, but too much can lead to burnout. The goal is balance:

  • Communicate clearly and early
  • Set realistic timelines
  • Support teams with the training and structure they need

Employees need to feel equipped—not overwhelmed—by the pace of change. Without that preparation, even the most powerful platform will fall short of expectations.

Why Executive Buy-In Changes Everything

Top-down support isn’t optional. Leaders need to:

  • Clearly articulate the vision and value of the change
  • Connect the change to team and departmental impact
  • Reinforce the message through every phase of execution

When leaders speak with clarity and consistency, it creates alignment at all levels. Without that, adoption suffers and silos persist.

Inside the Blueprinting Workshop

M&S’s Process Impact Blueprinting Workshop is a two-and-a-half day session that brings together stakeholders from across the organization to:

  • Identify pain points and inefficiencies
  • Map upstream and downstream dependencies
  • Define future-state processes and high-level requirements

The workshop builds shared understanding across departments, breaks down silos, and energizes teams to move forward together. It also helps project teams prioritize and sequence work, identifying what can be improved now and what’s needed in the long term.

Short-Term Wins Keep Change Alive

Long-term transformation requires near-term momentum. Setting clear, measurable short-term wins:

  • Builds morale and engagement
  • Provides visible proof that change is working
  • Fuels broader adoption and organizational trust

These wins are especially important when the larger project horizon is long and complex. Quick victories help people stay committed.

Facilitating Dialogue Across Silos

One of the most powerful outcomes of the blueprinting workshop is getting the right people in the room. That includes:

  • Enthusiastic problem-solvers who know the process inside and out
  • Skeptics who may resist change but hold key knowledge

By inviting both, M&S helps organizations uncover the real reasons behind bottlenecks, friction, and confusion. When people understand how their work impacts others, it creates empathy—and that’s a major driver of change.

Measuring Success in Real Terms

Success isn’t just about system uptime or budget adherence. It’s about:

  • Quantitative metrics: wait times, first-time quality, data availability
  • Qualitative measures: user feedback, adoption rates, employee engagement

By tracking both, organizations get a clearer picture of what’s working—and what still needs attention.

From Reactive to Proactive

Blueprinting workshops help teams shift from firefighting to future-building. Instead of reacting to broken systems or unmet needs, they:

  • Design with intent
  • Focus on innovation
  • Build alignment across functions

This shift leads to faster project timelines, more confident decision-making, and ultimately, greater ROI.

item.title: Human Coded 017: Why Great Technology Still Fails Without the Right People Behind It
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Technology as an Enabler, Not the Driver

Technology is often seen as the hero in change initiatives. But as Casey Zaitz and Ashok Aggarwal explain in this episode of Human-Coded, technology on its own rarely drives success. It’s the people, the processes, and the culture around that technology that determine whether it thrives or fails.

Successful transformation happens when tech is aligned with a broader strategy for adoption, training, communication, and ongoing support. Technology is the enabler—not the driver—of change.

Lessons from the Field: Real-World Change Failures and Fixes

Casey shares insight from mergers and acquisitions work, where companies must quickly adapt to new platforms, processes, and structures. Success didn’t come from flawless IT integration—it came from supporting people through abrupt organizational change.

Ashok outlines a case where a failed Salesforce implementation was turned around—not by changing the tool, but by shifting the approach to people. When M&S stepped in, the tech stayed the same, but the outcome was completely different because adoption was prioritized.

In both examples, it was never the software that was the issue—it was how the change was managed.

The Challenge of AI Adoption

Generative AI is one of the most powerful technologies available today. It’s easy to use, useful, and intuitive. Yet most organizations haven’t adopted it at scale. Why? Because change management hasn’t caught up.

Tools like Braided AI exist to solve that very issue: helping teams deploy and adopt generative AI across the org, safely and securely. The gap isn’t capability—it’s communication, training, and leadership alignment.

Cross-Department Communication is Critical

Rolling out a technology change isn’t just about configuring software. It’s about:

  • Explaining the why and how to every affected user
  • Helping people understand how their work impacts others
  • Establishing a shared vision for how the technology will help
  • Identifying pain points across departments before go-live

Communication breakdowns lead to slow adoption, rework, and resistance. Cross-functional alignment is the antidote.

Strategic Over Tactical: Focus on What Matters

Just because a tool is powerful doesn’t mean it’s the right tool for the moment. Casey notes that sometimes a spreadsheet is still the best option. Real transformation is not about flash—it’s about utility.

Before choosing a tech stack, M&S helps clients ask:

  • Will this help people do their jobs better?
  • Can we support and sustain its usage over time?
  • How will this impact upstream and downstream processes?
  • What training, communication, and cultural shifts are required?

When the answers are clear, the technology succeeds. When they’re not, the initiative falters—no matter how advanced the tool.

Adoption Over Installation

Ashok summarizes it well: the hardest part of technology change isn’t the implementation. It’s changing how thousands of people think, work, and adapt.

If a solution is delivered but not used, it isn’t a solution. If it’s used poorly or inconsistently, it creates more friction than progress.

At M&S, that’s why every technology change initiative includes:

  • Stakeholder alignment at every level
  • Tailored communication strategies
  • Empathetic rollout planning
  • Post-launch support and iteration

item.title: Human Coded 018: The Story of the Appalachian Software Factory
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
A New Kind of Software Model

The Appalachian Software Factory (ASF) isn’t your typical dev shop. Built by a team of makers, tinkerers, and problem-solvers, ASF offers custom software solutions for enterprise clients, government partners, and growing startups—all from the mountains of West Virginia.

What makes ASF different is the dual-focus model:

  • Client work: Delivering robust custom software, dashboards, tooling, and analytics solutions to organizations of all sizes.
  • Startup incubation: Giving team members the opportunity to launch their own ideas—with equity, mentorship, and real-world experience built in.

This blend of service and product creation fuels deep skill development and builds talent that’s versatile, entrepreneurial, and impact-driven.

Why Appalachia?

There’s a deep craftsman spirit in Appalachia. ASF taps into that legacy by creating space for coders, designers, and builders who want to stay rooted in the region while working on cutting-edge technology.

  • Strong university pipeline (especially in Morgantown)
  • High quality of life and natural beauty
  • Historically overlooked but rich in problem-solving and craftsmanship

The result is a growing ecosystem of homegrown talent—people who want to live where they love and build things that matter.

A Flexible Approach to Software Delivery

ASF doesn’t believe in one-size-fits-all. Depending on the client, the team might:

  • Build new applications from scratch (greenfield development)
  • Join enterprise teams to maintain and expand legacy systems
  • Integrate with existing product teams for feature enhancements or problem-solving

Rather than giant, months-long builds, ASF emphasizes an iterative, MVP-first approach. Every project starts with a deep understanding of the user, their needs, and the business value of the solution. Then comes rapid development, hands-on feedback, and continuous improvement.

Human Impact Through Code

For ASF, success isn’t about lines of code—it’s about leverage. If a week of dev work can save thousands of hours across a client’s workforce, that’s a win. If a new tool helps reduce error rates, improve decision-making, or streamline an essential process, the impact is real.

Custom software isn’t just a tech solution. It’s a tool that solves human problems—often at scale.

Innovation from the Inside Out

ASF has already launched and supported several impactful ventures, including:

  • Momentum: A greenhouse operations platform that tracks labor, logistics, and timing in plant production. It’s helping growers manage complexity and scale with precision.
  • Upcoming startup (in stealth): A productivity tool built around smart clipboard functionality, leveraging contextual AI to automate common actions and accelerate workflows.

These ventures aren’t side projects. They’re built and supported by the same talent delivering top-tier solutions for clients—proof that ASF’s internal model cultivates innovation.

Looking Ahead

The vision for ASF is clear: more builders, more ventures, more impact. The team is expanding, the pipeline is growing, and the possibilities are wide open.

ASF is proving that world-class software can come from anywhere—and that Appalachia is a place where technology and craftsmanship meet.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
As businesses navigate the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), it becomes increasingly crucial to assess how AI can be effectively integrated into their strategies. AI is not a one-size-fits-all solution; rather, it should be seen as an extension of a company’s existing technological framework, enhancing current capabilities and adding value to strategic objectives.

Aligning AI with Business Strategy

To integrate AI effectively, businesses should start by ensuring that their existing technology plans and infrastructure are robust. AI is not a standalone tool; it must build on a foundation of reliable data and secure networks. Companies should first evaluate their current systems to ensure that they are capable of supporting AI. This includes having standardized data and effective reporting mechanisms in place. If a company struggles to provide accurate data to its management team, AI won’t be the solution to these underlying issues.

The next step is to identify specific objectives that AI can help achieve. These goals should be rooted in the company’s overall business strategy. Whether it’s enhancing customer experience, streamlining operations, or driving data-driven decisions, clear objectives are essential. AI is most effective when it complements existing strategies, acting as a catalyst rather than a replacement.

Navigating the Regulatory Environment

The regulatory landscape for AI is complex and varies by industry and region. However, businesses must take a proactive approach to understanding and complying with these regulations. The European AI Act, for example, places significant responsibility on organizations to ensure their AI systems meet ethical and privacy standards. This responsibility cannot be shifted onto vendors; businesses must rigorously test and validate their AI solutions before deployment.

Understanding the level of risk associated with AI systems is also critical. High-risk AI systems, particularly those used in healthcare, education, or law enforcement, require stringent oversight and governance. Compliance should not be viewed as a mere tick-box exercise; instead, it’s an opportunity to build trust and establish a reputation for ethical AI practices. This involves not only meeting regulatory requirements but also fostering a culture of transparency and inclusivity in AI development.

Implementing AI with Ethical Considerations

Successful AI integration requires a multi-faceted approach that includes design, testing, and continuous monitoring. During the design phase, it’s essential to involve a diverse group of stakeholders who represent the various groups impacted by the AI system. This ensures that the system is designed with a broad perspective, addressing potential biases and ethical concerns from the outset.

Rigorous testing is crucial to identify and mitigate any issues before deployment. Unlike traditional systems, AI requires a more nuanced approach to testing, as it must account for the different ways users may interact with the system. Continuous monitoring post-deployment is equally important. AI systems must adapt to changing environments and usage patterns, ensuring they remain effective and reliable over time.

Building a Trustworthy AI Framework

AI implementation is similar to information security in many ways. Both require a risk-based approach, early involvement of key stakeholders, and a commitment to ongoing governance and monitoring. For AI, this means developing clear policies and guidelines around its use, ensuring ethical considerations are embedded in the process, and maintaining oversight to prevent issues as the business environment evolves.

Integrating AI into your business strategy isn’t just about adopting the latest technology—it's about setting the stage for a transformative journey. As you navigate this dynamic landscape, remember that AI is a powerful ally that can elevate your capabilities and drive meaningful progress. It’s not about replacing what works; it’s about enhancing and expanding what’s possible.

By aligning AI with your strategic goals, staying ahead of regulatory requirements, and embedding ethical considerations into every phase, you’re not just adopting a tool—you’re championing a future where technology and humanity thrive together. Embrace this opportunity to redefine your approach, drive innovation, and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

Let’s transform the future together. Reach out to us to explore how AI can align with your unique vision and propel your business towards unprecedented success. Our team is here to guide you through every step, ensuring that your AI journey is as impactful and rewarding as it can be. 

Ready to make AI a game-changer for your business? Contact us today to start a conversation about how we can help you integrate AI in a way that’s strategic, ethical, and uniquely tailored to your needs.

item.title: Human Coded 019: Monarch Learning Labs and the Future of Hands-On Learning
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Rethinking Training in High-Stakes Industries

Monarch Learning Labs is a venture designed to solve a common pain point in medical devices and advanced manufacturing: training. When the tools are complex and the stakes are high, traditional approaches like manuals, videos, or on-site demos fall short.

Monarch creates immersive, interactive simulations that mimic the exact interface and behavior of the real device or system—without needing access to the physical hardware. This creates a low-risk, high-fidelity training environment that improves learning outcomes while reducing cost and logistics challenges.

Built for Complexity, Designed for Scale

Industries like healthcare and manufacturing depend on teams being able to use powerful, technical equipment with confidence and precision. Monarch was built with that reality in mind.

Its platform includes:

  • Digital twin interfaces that mirror the look, feel, and function of real-world systems
  • Integrated learning management tools to track progress, issue credentials, and personalize training paths
  • Scalable delivery from anywhere with an internet connection
  • Support for multiple use cases, from new user training to sales demos and internal certification

The result is a training experience that meets modern learners where they are—whether they’re on the factory floor, in a hospital system, or onboarding remotely.

Tangible Benefits for Businesses and Learners

For decision-makers, Monarch reduces time, cost, and friction in training rollout:

  • Avoid flying people across the country
  • Keep mission-critical equipment in operation instead of tied up for training
  • Update training modules instantly as tech evolves

For learners, the benefits are just as strong:

  • Practice in a safe, judgment-free environment
  • Get more repetitions with fewer constraints
  • Learn new systems or refresh knowledge at their own pace

Whether you’re onboarding new hires or rolling out software updates across hundreds of users, Monarch gives both the trainer and the trainee more flexibility and control.

Designed by Engineers Who’ve Been There

Both Jeremy Kimmel and Jimmy Lutz, co-founders of Monarch Learning Labs, bring firsthand experience in medical devices and enterprise delivery. They understand the frustration of limited resources, the risk of poor training, and the slow pace of adoption when clinicians or operators aren’t confident in new tools.

Monarch is rooted in their belief that training should not be a barrier to innovation. By delivering high-fidelity, dynamic simulations through modern software, they’re lowering that barrier across industries.

More Than Just Compliance

Training isn’t just about ticking a box—it’s about enabling transformation. Monarch is already in use in clinical settings where better training means better patient outcomes. It’s also making waves in advanced manufacturing, where uptime and efficiency matter more than ever.

As technologies grow more complex and interconnected, organizations need a better way to help their teams adapt. Monarch is building that future—one interface at a time.

item.title: Human Coded 020: How GTD Speech Is Giving Time Back to Speech Therapists
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Solving a Real Need in the Therapy Room

GTD Speech is a new venture built from firsthand experience. Created by speech-language pathologist Julie Bearden, the platform addresses a daily challenge in the profession: how to track and respond to speech sounds accurately, in real time, without losing momentum during a session.

Speech therapists are often juggling documentation, data collection, and engagement with their clients—especially in pediatric settings or virtual sessions. GTD Speech introduces a tool that listens in, transcribes in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), and helps therapists identify whether a sound was correct or not, on the spot.

What Makes GTD Speech Different

This isn’t another generic speech-to-text app. It’s tailored to the unique needs of SLPs:

  • Real-time phonetic transcription using IPA
  • Designed for both in-person and teletherapy environments
  • Identifies sounds in isolation (not just words)
  • Flags correct or incorrect pronunciations automatically
  • Built alongside real therapists, with ongoing feedback and iteration

Where traditional transcription tools might autocorrect or skip over subtle mispronunciations, GTD Speech captures what actually happened—because that’s what matters in speech therapy.

Backed by Data, Built with Empathy

Julie surveyed over 200 therapists during early development. The findings were clear:

  • 72% said they don’t have time to transcribe during sessions
  • 96% of teletherapists said they have trouble clearly hearing client speech sounds
  • 59% of in-person therapists reported similar hearing difficulties

That’s not a technology issue—it’s a human one. And GTD Speech is here to help therapists stay present with their clients, reduce documentation burdens, and make every session more effective.

A Platform in the Making

Right now, GTD Speech is in beta—and Julie is calling on her peers to help shape what comes next. From live feedback on features to ideas for future capabilities, the platform is designed to grow with the profession.

Speech therapists can expect a platform that respects their expertise and supports their goals, not one that replaces clinical judgment. GTD Speech is a tool that works in the background so the therapist can focus on what matters most: helping clients communicate.

item.title: Human Coded 021: Exploring the Innovation Behind InnovAgents - Building User-Friendly Salesforce Apps
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Turning Internal Tools into Scalable Solutions

InnovAgents is a venture born out of necessity. After years of delivering Salesforce consulting projects, the team repeatedly ran into the same issues—missing features, clunky workflows, and common pain points across clients. Instead of continuing to build custom solutions for each engagement, they started building apps that could scale.

The result? A suite of Salesforce-native tools that feel like part of the platform, not bolted onto it.

What Makes InnovAgents Apps Different

Most apps on the Salesforce AppExchange fall into two camps: side projects by solo developers, or visibility plays from consulting firms. InnovAgents is doing something different. Each product is:

  • Purpose-built to address widespread gaps observed across many implementations
  • Developed natively inside Salesforce for a seamless user experience
  • Continuously improved based on real feedback from early users
  • Supported by a dedicated team with product discipline and customer care

From design to delivery, these apps are made to feel like Salesforce itself built them.

Built Around Real User Pain

The team doesn’t chase shiny ideas. Instead, they validate needs through hands-on experience, data, and patterns seen in client work. For example:

  • Splash Announcements started as an internal tool to notify users about new releases. Every client asked for customization and urgency controls—so those became core features.
  • FundOps grew from conversations with entrepreneurship networks in West Virginia. The team saw firsthand how fragmented the funding process was, and built a central collaboration tool for founders, investors, and ecosystem partners.

This feedback loop is at the heart of every release.

The Value of Going Native

Why build natively in Salesforce? Because speed matters. Usability matters. Familiarity matters. InnovAgents apps avoid popups, modals, or unnecessary integrations. They feel like part of the platform and require little to no learning curve.

The apps stand out not just because of what they do—but how they do it:

  • Faster load times and seamless data access
  • Lower total cost of ownership
  • Simple, intuitive interfaces
  • Easier adoption by teams already working in Salesforce

Staying Ahead in a Fast-Moving Ecosystem

Salesforce is always evolving. Rather than compete, InnovAgents complements. As Salesforce focuses on large-scale innovation and broad capabilities, it often leaves smaller usability gaps untouched. InnovAgents moves quickly to address those gaps—while keeping prices accessible and user needs front and center.

This makes InnovAgents an asset to the Salesforce ecosystem, not a competitor. They're paving the roads that connect the platform’s highways.

item.title: Human Coded 022: Transforming Business Workflows - A Deep Dive into Braided
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
AI That Works the Way Teams Do

Most AI tools today are built for solo users. You open a chat, ask a question, get a response, and move on. But that’s not how most teams operate.

Braided flips the script by creating a shared space where business teams can:

  • Collaborate in real time with AI
  • Share prompts and outputs across departments
  • Compare results from multiple language models side by side

Instead of scattered tools and inconsistent workflows, Braided brings clarity and cohesion to how teams explore, prompt, and problem-solve with AI.

Built to Bridge Gaps in the AI Landscape

The Braided team came together with a clear mission: make enterprise-grade AI usable, shareable, and secure. Their backgrounds in machine learning, systems architecture, and business strategy shaped the product in powerful ways:

  • Jay Mason saw a need for a secure way to bring multiple models into one tool without vendor lock-in.
  • John McCauley designed Braided to stay ahead of the fast-changing AI ecosystem with plug-and-play flexibility.
  • Jared Icenhower focused on making AI accessible to everyday business users—not just tech insiders.

With Braided, teams don’t have to choose just one AI model. They can:

  • Switch between models like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and more within the same conversation
  • Tailor prompts to specific outcomes and compare how each model performs
  • Use AI as a shared teammate in brainstorming, writing, analysis, and planning

Addressing Real Business Concerns

Security and compliance are top of mind for IT leaders. Braided meets those concerns head-on:

  • Enterprise-ready platform with vetted model integrations
  • Prompts and responses are never used to train external models
  • Controlled environment to prevent data leakage from copy/paste habits

The result? A safer, more centralized way to scale AI use across teams without compromising sensitive business data.

Designed for the 90%, Not the Niche

Braided doesn’t aim to be everything for everyone. Instead, it delivers high-impact features for business users who want to:

  • Draft reports, emails, or documentation faster
  • Summarize research and meeting notes
  • Solve problems collaboratively without losing context

Rather than chasing trends, the product is shaped by user needs. Biweekly updates ensure Braided evolves based on what matters most to its community.

What’s Next: Agents and Customization

On the roadmap:

  • Agentic AI Support: Custom agents that can perform tasks like generating Google Docs with pre-formatted sections or querying enterprise data.
  • Meta Instructions & Prompt Templates: Project-level settings that save time and ensure consistency across every AI interaction.
  • A Braided-Owned AI Model: A secure, controllable alternative for sensitive use cases that require more tailored outputs and data handling.

These features all push Braided closer to becoming the intelligent backbone of modern business collaboration.

The Value of Going Native

Why build natively in Salesforce? Because speed matters. Usability matters. Familiarity matters. InnovAgents apps avoid popups, modals, or unnecessary integrations. They feel like part of the platform and require little to no learning curve.

The apps stand out not just because of what they do—but how they do it:

  • Faster load times and seamless data access
  • Lower total cost of ownership
  • Simple, intuitive interfaces
  • Easier adoption by teams already working in Salesforce

Staying Ahead in a Fast-Moving Ecosystem

Salesforce is always evolving. Rather than compete, InnovAgents complements. As Salesforce focuses on large-scale innovation and broad capabilities, it often leaves smaller usability gaps untouched. InnovAgents moves quickly to address those gaps—while keeping prices accessible and user needs front and center.

This makes InnovAgents an asset to the Salesforce ecosystem, not a competitor. They're paving the roads that connect the platform’s highways.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
As businesses navigate the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), it becomes increasingly crucial to assess how AI can be effectively integrated into their strategies. AI is not a one-size-fits-all solution; rather, it should be seen as an extension of a company’s existing technological framework, enhancing current capabilities and adding value to strategic objectives.

Aligning AI with Business Strategy

To integrate AI effectively, businesses should start by ensuring that their existing technology plans and infrastructure are robust. AI is not a standalone tool; it must build on a foundation of reliable data and secure networks. Companies should first evaluate their current systems to ensure that they are capable of supporting AI. This includes having standardized data and effective reporting mechanisms in place. If a company struggles to provide accurate data to its management team, AI won’t be the solution to these underlying issues.

The next step is to identify specific objectives that AI can help achieve. These goals should be rooted in the company’s overall business strategy. Whether it’s enhancing customer experience, streamlining operations, or driving data-driven decisions, clear objectives are essential. AI is most effective when it complements existing strategies, acting as a catalyst rather than a replacement.

Navigating the Regulatory Environment

The regulatory landscape for AI is complex and varies by industry and region. However, businesses must take a proactive approach to understanding and complying with these regulations. The European AI Act, for example, places significant responsibility on organizations to ensure their AI systems meet ethical and privacy standards. This responsibility cannot be shifted onto vendors; businesses must rigorously test and validate their AI solutions before deployment.

Understanding the level of risk associated with AI systems is also critical. High-risk AI systems, particularly those used in healthcare, education, or law enforcement, require stringent oversight and governance. Compliance should not be viewed as a mere tick-box exercise; instead, it’s an opportunity to build trust and establish a reputation for ethical AI practices. This involves not only meeting regulatory requirements but also fostering a culture of transparency and inclusivity in AI development.

Implementing AI with Ethical Considerations

Successful AI integration requires a multi-faceted approach that includes design, testing, and continuous monitoring. During the design phase, it’s essential to involve a diverse group of stakeholders who represent the various groups impacted by the AI system. This ensures that the system is designed with a broad perspective, addressing potential biases and ethical concerns from the outset.

Rigorous testing is crucial to identify and mitigate any issues before deployment. Unlike traditional systems, AI requires a more nuanced approach to testing, as it must account for the different ways users may interact with the system. Continuous monitoring post-deployment is equally important. AI systems must adapt to changing environments and usage patterns, ensuring they remain effective and reliable over time.

Building a Trustworthy AI Framework

AI implementation is similar to information security in many ways. Both require a risk-based approach, early involvement of key stakeholders, and a commitment to ongoing governance and monitoring. For AI, this means developing clear policies and guidelines around its use, ensuring ethical considerations are embedded in the process, and maintaining oversight to prevent issues as the business environment evolves.

Integrating AI into your business strategy isn’t just about adopting the latest technology—it's about setting the stage for a transformative journey. As you navigate this dynamic landscape, remember that AI is a powerful ally that can elevate your capabilities and drive meaningful progress. It’s not about replacing what works; it’s about enhancing and expanding what’s possible.

By aligning AI with your strategic goals, staying ahead of regulatory requirements, and embedding ethical considerations into every phase, you’re not just adopting a tool—you’re championing a future where technology and humanity thrive together. Embrace this opportunity to redefine your approach, drive innovation, and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

item.title: Human Coded 023: Revolutionizing Wayfinding - Following the Journey of get2there
item.dc:creator: quinn.brewer
item.content:encoded:
Solving a Universal Problem: Getting Lost

Everyone has experienced the frustration of showing up somewhere new and having no idea where to go. Whether it’s a college campus, hospital, corporate complex, or event venue, the stress of poor wayfinding can negatively impact how people feel about your organization.

get2there aims to solve that. It’s a digital map platform designed to help people navigate unfamiliar environments with ease—without needing to download an app or decode a static PDF.

Designed for Visitors, Managed with Ease

Unlike traditional maps or kiosks, get2there provides:

  • QR-code access, no downloads required
  • Searchable maps tailored to each location
  • Real-time updates and customization for events or temporary changes

From finding a meeting room to navigating a multi-use sports complex, the experience is intuitive and user-first. Visitors can search by name, category, or keyword—whether they’re looking for a restroom or a retail store.

And for the facilities team? The lift is light. Organizations simply provide existing map files and information, and the get2there team builds and manages the experience. Updates are handled collaboratively, ensuring maps stay accurate without requiring in-house development resources.

More Than Maps: Supporting Better Experiences

get2there isn't just about directions. It’s about:

  • Reducing visitor stress and confusion
  • Improving staff efficiency by lowering the need for manual wayfinding help
  • Enhancing overall guest experience, especially in high-pressure environments like hospitals or arenas

Organizations can also use get2there to:

  • Track usage trends through analytics
  • Provide accessibility information
  • Monetize event-specific maps or sponsorships

Where It Fits Best

While any space with foot traffic can benefit from get2there, early traction is especially strong in:

  • Healthcare and hospitals
  • College and university campuses
  • Large corporate offices and training centers
  • Convention centers and resort properties
  • Mixed-use complexes (retail, sports, government, and residential)

It’s particularly useful for organizations that want a better guest experience but lack the internal tech team to build their own tools.

Looking Ahead

CEO Taryn Quinlan brings 25+ years of go-to-market experience and customer empathy to the table. Under her leadership, get2there is building for the future with:

  • Smarter integrations (like traffic flow data and location-based services)
  • Visitor analytics and insights to support better decision-making
  • Tools to unlock new revenue streams through map sponsorship or premium experiences

The goal isn’t just to make better maps. It’s to help organizations meet modern expectations and deliver a smoother, more thoughtful experience to every guest.

item.title: Unlocking the Hidden Power of Your Law Firm's Data
item.dc:creator: LeoTome
item.content:encoded:
If you ask most law firms whether they "use data," they'll likely say yes. After all, every firm tracks billable hours and case outcomes, right?

But here’s the truth: simply having data isn’t the same as being a data-driven firm.

Being truly data-driven means treating your data like a strategic asset that informs decisions, fuels innovation, and gives you a real competitive edge.

And in today's legal landscape, firms that master this shift aren't just surviving, they're thriving.

What Being Data-Driven Really Means for Law Firms

In a data-driven law firm, information isn't siloed in different systems, hidden in dusty files, or trapped in the memories of senior partners.

Instead, data is accessible, organized, analyzed, and actively used to guide:

  • Strategic decisions (Which practice areas are growing fastest?)
  • Client service improvements (Where are bottlenecks in the intake process?)
  • Financial planning (Which types of cases generate the best margins?)
  • Risk management (Where are potential compliance gaps?)

Data-driven firms don't just react to problems—they anticipate them.

How Data Can Transform Legal Services

I've seen firsthand how powerful this shift can be.

  • Predictive Analytics: Firms use historical litigation data to predict case outcomes, helping clients make smarter decisions about settlements and trial strategies.
  • Document Automation: Instead of drafting the same types of contracts or filings from scratch every time, firms use data templates that speed up production without sacrificing quality.
  • Client Insights: By analyzing client behavior patterns, firms can tailor communication, predict future needs, and deliver a more personalized client experience.

The result? Faster service, better outcomes, happier clients, and stronger profitability.

Building a Robust Data Strategy

Becoming truly data-driven doesn’t happen by accident. It takes a thoughtful strategy.

Here’s the playbook I recommend:

  • Centralize your data: Integrate systems so data flows between case management, CRM, billing, and other tools.
  • Clean your data: Standardize and scrub existing data to eliminate errors, redundancies, and gaps.
  • Secure your data: Implement strong data governance and cybersecurity measures, which are especially important in a world of rising privacy regulations.
  • Analyze your data: Invest in analytics tools and people who can turn raw numbers into actionable insights.
  • Act on your data: Build a culture where insights lead to fundamental operational and strategic changes, not just reports that sit in someone's inbox.

Overcoming Common Data Challenges

Let’s be real, building a data-driven culture isn’t easy.

Some of the biggest hurdles I see firms face include:

  • Legacy Systems: Outdated software that doesn't talk to other platforms.
  • Data Silos: Different departments hoarding their own data.
  • Poor Data Quality: Inconsistent or incomplete information that undermines trust.
  • Change Resistance: Lawyers and staff reluctant to embrace new, data-driven ways of working.

The key is to tackle these challenges head-on, starting small if necessary, and celebrating early wins to build momentum.

Why Data + AI Is a Game Changer

Data is powerful on its own.

But when you combine it with Artificial Intelligence (AI)? That’s where transformation really accelerates.

Imagine AI tools that can:

  • Flag potential issues in a contract before a lawyer even reads it.
  • Suggest optimal legal strategies based on case law analysis.
  • Prioritize leads or client matters based on predicted revenue potential.

Data + AI doesn't replace great lawyers, it frees them to do more high-value work, faster and smarter.

Final Thoughts

Law firms that become data-driven don't just "keep up" with competitors, they leap ahead.

They:

  • Make better strategic decisions.
  • Deliver more responsive and customized client services.
  • Drive higher profitability with greater efficiency.
  • Future-proof themselves against disruption.

In the next post, we'll take a deeper look at how AI is already reshaping legal workflows, and how your firm can start leveraging it today.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
There’s a moment I’ve come to expect in nearly every client engagement. Someone walks into our workshop, drops into their chair with a sigh, and says something like, “Can’t wait to talk about the same problems again. This’ll be fun.”

I love that moment.

Not because I enjoy pain (I’m not a monster), but because I know what’s coming next. By the end of the day, that same person will say, “We’ve accomplished more in this one session than we have in the past year.” And that—right there—is why I love what I do.

I lead M&S Consulting’s Project Management as a Service and Organizational Transformation practice, which is just a fancy way of saying: I help organizations get real about how they work, what needs to change, and how to actually make it happen. It’s not about flashy tech or buzzwords. It’s about people—and creating space for them to do their best work in systems that actually support them.

Let’s talk about what really makes change successful (and what definitely doesn’t).

Urgency Is Not a Fire Drill

We hear a lot about the need to “create urgency” for change. And yes, urgency matters—but not the kind that leads to panic, burnout, or forcing people to white-knuckle their way through another chaotic rollout.

Creating urgency without breaking your team starts with clarity. Clear communication, early and often. Realistic timelines. Leadership that actually leads. It’s the difference between lighting a spark and setting the building on fire.

I often compare it to putting someone behind the wheel of a Porsche and not explaining where the brakes are. Sure, it’s shiny and fast. But if your people aren’t prepared to drive the new system, you’re not enabling innovation—you’re creating frustration.

Adoption doesn’t happen by accident. It’s the result of thoughtful, well-paced change that puts humans first.

The Power of a Room Full of People Who’ve Never Talked Before

Enter: our Process Impact Blueprinting Workshop.

This is where things get real. We gather key people from across the organization—sales, ops, customer service, business intelligence, and yes, the skeptics who think this is all a waste of time. And we get them talking. Really talking.

The workshop is designed to surface the pain points, inefficiencies, and “I didn’t know you needed that” moments that keep organizations stuck. And because we open with an executive stakeholder sharing the why, people don’t sit around wondering why they gave up three hours of their day. They know the purpose—and they begin to see the path forward.

The workshop isn’t just about gathering requirements. It’s about aligning people. When you bring together high flyers (who know every process inside and out) and skeptics (who’ve seen it all before and are waiting for the next initiative to crash and burn), something powerful happens. Those differing perspectives spark better solutions—and often, the skeptics become the biggest champions of the change. Why? Because they were finally invited into the conversation.

Change Doesn’t Work Without People (Sorry, It Just Doesn’t)

Here’s the most common mistake I see: companies invest tons of money in tech, tools, and process design—then skip the training, testing, and communication that actually brings people along for the ride.

You can have the best software in the world, but if your people don’t understand it, trust it, or feel included in the transition? It’s not going to stick.

We talk a lot about user acceptance testing and training timelines in our practice—not because we’re obsessed with checklists, but because we’ve seen what happens when those steps are rushed or ignored. Change fatigue sets in. Adoption drops off. And eventually, the bright shiny thing becomes shelfware.

Change requires humans. Not just at the end, but from the beginning. When employees feel seen, heard, and empowered to contribute—they show up differently. They take ownership. They get excited. That’s where transformation takes root.

Success Is Measurable (And Sometimes Surprising)

One of the questions I get asked all the time: “How will we know if this is working?”

We measure success from two angles: quantitative and qualitative.


On the numbers side, we look at things like wait times, first-time quality, handoff delays—process metrics that give us real insight into efficiency gains. You’d be amazed how many teams are shocked by how low their first-time quality rates are. (Spoiler: It’s rarely the people’s fault. It’s the process.)

But we also listen to what people are saying. What does engagement look like? Are folks actually using the new system? Do they feel confident, or confused? Are there new ideas bubbling up from teams who feel empowered?

That mix of data and human insight paints a full picture—and helps teams keep iterating long after the go-live celebration cake has been eaten.

Why the Blueprint Matters More Than the Build

One last thing I want to leave you with: you wouldn’t build a house without a blueprint. So why are so many organizations trying to redesign critical systems by gut feel?

Our workshops provide the foundation—aligning vision, surfacing pain points, and defining high-level requirements so your team can actually move forward together. You stop reacting to every fire, and start designing for the future.

And the best part? You get that momentum before you start burning through project hours. You shorten timelines, avoid backtracking, and prevent the kind of scope creep that makes everyone want to cry quietly in the break room.

When organizations pause to create a thoughtful blueprint, they unlock something better than process improvement: shared ownership. And that, more than any tech tool or feature list, is what makes change succeed.

At M&S Consulting, we don’t believe in change for change’s sake. We believe in transformation that honors the people doing the work, equips them for success, and builds something stronger, smarter, and more sustainable.

So if you’re ready to stop duct-taping solutions together and actually build something that works, let’s talk. I’ll bring the blueprint.
